prior_findings.evidence: hasCompiledEntry explicitly unwraps RistrettoMethod or InterpreterResolvedJavaMethod and requires a holder, nonnull resolved pointer, and inequality to InterpreterKnownCompiledEntryPoints.getMethodNotCompiledHandler(). This is the same callability predicate used by InterpreterToVM.shouldCallAOTEntryPoint. Both raw and wrapped actual sentinel metadata are rejected by the new native test.

analysis: Unknown ResolvedJavaMethod implementations now fail closed without catching broad compiler invariant exceptions. A missing holder short-circuits safely; a null or sentinel pointer does not enable fallback. No change to the existing permanent bailout after a failed guard.

The GraalDirectives and RistrettoDirectives exclusions precede the fallback. The new payload executes inRuntimeCompiledCode inside the protected range and requires compiled success/catch results, validating the preserved semantic-marker behavior.

Returning false from tryInvocationPlugin feeds the existing ordinary invoke/inline path. BytecodeParser builds INCLUDE_AND_HANDLE edges for CheckAll and ExplicitOnly modes; its default Profile mode also retains the edge because RistrettoProfilingInfo.getExceptionSeen returns UNKNOWN. Only direct invocations reach tryInvocationPlugin, after target resolution, so eligibility is checked on the actual direct target.

The normal native target lowerings continue consuming the same interpreter entry point now checked by the guard. Actual Object.clone success and CloneNotSupportedException behavior are tested from runtime-loaded bytecode with graph, installation, and runtime-execution assertions.

Reviewed required runtime plugin registrations (Object.clone/hashCode, System.identityHashCode/getSecurityManager, Unsafe.allocateInstance, Class.desiredAssertionStatus, MethodHandles.lookup) and ordinary plugin semantics. Required registration is not by itself proof of a safe body, but no concrete invalid callable AOT body was found in the registered production set. Directive bodies remain excluded.

Caller-sensitive MethodHandles.lookup was challenged separately: the fallback body uses Reflection.getCallerClass; its substitution performs a source stackwalk, and JavaStackFrameVisitor documents and implements translation through InterpreterSupport for Ristretto frame metadata. RuntimeCodeInstaller source-ID gaps therefore do not themselves imply a wrong caller. The existing lookup plugin can also decline handling ignored security-stackwalk callers. No concrete caller-sensitive regression was established.

Test payload classes are loaded from registered bytes through a fresh loader; loader identity is asserted. Warmup checks interpreter execution, then parseOnly checks the ordinary clone exception node, compileAndInstallInCrema checks live installed code and publication, and post-install execution checks distinct clone/class/field values plus the compiled catch marker. These assertions are materially stronger than an unobserved JIT warmup smoke.

The sentinel fixture is registered as queried only and uses a property-derived runtime method name, preventing the lookup itself from making the target invocable at image build time. It asserts the actual not-compiled pointer before testing both metadata forms.

nonblocking_observations.description: The sentinel test exercises the private eligibility helper, not an actual required-plugin invocation producing PermanentBailoutException. It strongly detects the original unsafe-holder predicate, while preservation of the bailout is source-reviewed. An end-to-end negative parser fixture would strengthen future regression coverage.

A runtime-loaded MethodHandles.lookup() protected-range test checking lookupClass and private access would broaden coverage of the generic fallback beyond clone. This review found no demonstrated defect requiring it as a blocker.
